finding: At 9:38 p.m. on 8 November 2026, three accessible stations had no working elevator to any train, and five more had lost one platform. About 15,600 Chicagoans lost their step-free half-mile walk to the ‘L’.

ledger.units: 9 elevator alerts at 8 stations; 2,746,388 residents (2020 Census) in 33,801 blocks
method: One pull of CTA’s active customer alerts at 21:38 Chicago time; impact "Elevator Status"
Alert text matched to the platforms (stops) of its station in the CTA stop list
Station scope: no step-free way to any platform; platform scope: one direction lost
Half-mile step-free walk on the OpenStreetMap network (extract of 2026-11-01), as Plate III
caveats: Alerts describe elevators in words; the platform match is a rule, checked by hand on each run
An outage is counted from the alert’s start; CTA does not publish when it is fixed, only that the alert ends
Ambulatory difficulty: ACS 2020-2024 tract estimates spread over blocks by population
Residents outside Chicago (Evanston, Skokie, Oak Park, Forest Park) are not counted
